title: Scope native System spacecraft-only lights to an actual light consumer

scope.subject: Keep the real native overlap, single renderer and exact close-world body material without a foreign lighting program recipe when spacecraft are absent.

research_summary: Exact #188/R3 software WebGL probe identifies two real MeshStandardMaterial shader recipes at the System/Approach overlap and release, incurring two ~1 s frames. Existing pinned BodyRenderer attaches ambient and directional lights for PBR spacecraft; procedural bodies explicitly shade independently, and this product-built StarSystem excludes spacecraft/trajectories. A disposable R3 bundle with the exact color/texture/material and spacecraft-only lights invisible in nonconsumer scenes passes all 3 unchanged fixed-deadline cases. Lambert reduced cost but changed every stable globe interior pixel (7.19 RGB MAE) and failed the strict 120 Hz boundary. A combined temporary atmosphere/cloud suppression also passed but removes authored detail, is unnecessary for this material-ownership change, and will not be promoted. Preserve actual paint, point lighting of prototype System, shader validation and CI budgets.

sources.finding: The pinned local MIT BodyRenderer constructor creates one directional and one ambient for PBR spacecraft; procedural surfaces use bespoke non-Three lighting uniforms.
Reuse installed Three Object3D.visible; invisible lights are never collected. Zero intensity still allocates the extra directional program recipe.
Exact hosted failure runs through native→Approach and retained carry under wide sample intervals. Keep explicit thresholds and readiness; remove unnecessary draw work.
Existing local production system filters spacecraft and trajectory data; retain an actual consumer guard and reuse existing per-system render scene.

search_ladder.conclusion: Keep the existing native and fallback System renderer paths.
Keep single Canvas and pass phase information through current React props.
Reuse Three visibility gating for light collection: an invisible light is not traversed; power zero alone still specializes a shader key.
Scope only the native per-system scene’s existing spacecraft-specific lights; retain them if an actual PBR model kind exists.

candidates.name: Existing Three visible flag for native PBR spacecraft lights, with consumer guard
candidates.source: Installed pinned Three 0.185.1 and local YEIS plus direct cold SwiftShader measurement
candidates.reason: No renderer, asset or material fork. Native directional/ambient lights with no spacecraft consumer do not affect independent close-world material program identity.

candidates.name: Per-presentation render pass
candidates.reason: Would add separate ownership and GL cost. Retain exact one-canvas renderer witness.

candidates.name: Substitute fallback globe diffuse material with Lambert
candidates.source: Disposable exact R3 A/B shadow on actual stable Approach raster
candidates.reason: Rendered globe pixels differ (7.19 average channel difference), and this alone did not close the 120 Hz native boundary. Preserve existing material and shader model.

decision.rationale: Remove only observed foreign native lighting from the standalone fallback shader. Preserve native star, atmosphere, clouds, light-correct spacecraft, globe material, input and actual paint.
decision.fallback: Keep isolated if native ordinary visuals or exact overlap pixels regress, or unchanged fixed-budget cases remain unstable.
